correctness.rationale: The proof gives exact finite prime bounds for every possible support size under \(\Omega(n)=5\), and the checker independently regenerates all \(121\) nondeficient integers. For each, the signed presentation is equivalent to a subset summing \(H(n)\); witnesses and all smaller cardinalities are checked exhaustively with integer arithmetic.

evidence: The 2026 finite-window record states that every odd nonsquare nondeficient \(n\le10^6\) has a presentation with at most seven negative coefficients.
All \(121\) integers in the present layer are at most \(442365\), so existence and a seven-sign upper bound are already covered.
broader_coverage.reasoning: That broader finite-window statement does not imply a five-sign sharp bound, exact minimum counts, the absence of minimum four, or the fifteen five-sign extremizers. The accepted claim is centered on those sharper quantities, not on existence alone.

evidence: The prior boundary item classifies the \(121\) odd nondeficient integers with \(\Omega(n)=5\) but contains no signed-presentation complexity claim.
Ross gives existence evidence below \(10^4\), Campbell gives a subset-sum criterion and counterexamples outside the layer, and the later window result gives at most seven negatives through \(10^6\).
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Combining those statements still does not determine the minimum subset cardinality for any of the \(121\) numbers, much less the complete spectrum. The new finite certificate supplies exactly that missing information.

evidence: Campbell Lemma 2.1 identifies \(H(n)=(\sigma(n)-2n)/2\) as a sum of distinct nontrivial proper divisors exactly when a \({-1,1}\)-presentation exists.
The present invariant minimizes the cardinality of that divisor subset, so it is a strict refinement of the existence formulation.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Equivalence of signed presentations and subset sums was treated as prior art. Novelty is claimed only for the exact minimum-cardinality spectrum on the specified multiplicity layer.

value.rationale: The minimum number of negative signs is a mathematically natural complexity measure of Ross presentations and directly sharpens a recent seven-sign finite-window result. Computing it on the first possible odd nondeficient multiplicity layer yields a canonical exact spectrum, a sharp maximum five, and a genuine missing value four rather than an arbitrary cutoff fact.
